title: DINOv3 · Global and local
question: Why can rising image-classification accuracy miss a dense-feature problem?
choices: CLS discrimination and patch coherence serve different needs.
Every patch must have the same vector.
Classification directly measures boundary accuracy.
Register tokens are annotation masks.
explanation: The report observes rising global accuracy alongside declining dense segmentation; patch similarity must also be checked.

title: DINOv3 · Masked targets
question: What does the iBOT branch predict?
choices: Raw RGB pixels only.
Teacher prototype distributions at student-masked patch positions.
Human segmentation masks.
The future Gram-teacher update time.
explanation: iBOT is latent-target reconstruction using an unmasked EMA-teacher view, not supervised mask prediction.

title: DINOv3 · Matrix dimensions
question: For P normalized patch vectors of width d, what is the patch Gram shape?
choices: d × d
P × d
P × P
One scalar per class
explanation: X has shape P × d; X Xᵀ compares every pair of patch positions, producing P × P.

title: DINOv3 · Coordinate freedom
question: Which change preserves a patch Gram matrix?
choices: Arbitrary independent changes to each patch.
Multiplying all features by 10 without normalization.
Deleting all patch positions.
The same orthogonal rotation applied to every patch vector.
explanation: A shared orthogonal Q obeys Q Qᵀ = I, so (XQ)(XQ)ᵀ = X Xᵀ.

title: DINOv3 · Loss arithmetic
question: If two symmetric Gram errors are each 0.6 and all others zero, what is the squared Frobenius loss?
explanation: Both off-diagonal entries count: 0.6² + 0.6² = 0.72. A mean reduction would have a different scale.

title: DINOv3 · Teacher clocks
question: How does the Gram teacher differ from the ordinary EMA teacher during refinement?
choices: Both receive supervised gradients.
Gram is fixed between discrete refreshes; EMA updates every step.
Gram updates every patch; EMA stays early forever.
They are two names for a single permanently identical model.
explanation: The Gram target begins at an early snapshot, then copies EMA every 10k steps, at most three updates in Appendix C.

title: DINOv3 · Frozen does not mean untrained
question: What does frozen-backbone linear probing still require?
choices: Updating the encoder on every target image.
Applying Gram loss at test time.
Training a prediction head with labeled downstream data.
A caption for every inference image.
explanation: The encoder is fixed, but the linear predictor and trained normalization use downstream supervision.

title: DINOv3 · Causal evidence
question: Why does the final DINOv3 versus DINOv2 table not isolate Gram anchoring?
choices: mIoU is always meaningless.
Both methods have identical data and architecture.
DINOv3 is evaluated only on its training labels.
Capacity, data and training recipe also differ.
explanation: The closer Figure 9 ablation varies anchoring settings; final-model comparisons change several factors at once.

title: V-JEPA 2.1 · Visible gradients
question: What is missing from masked-only V-JEPA supervision?
choices: Any gradients to the visible encoder tokens.
A direct location-specific prediction loss at visible output positions.
All temporal position information.
All learned teacher features.
explanation: Visible features already receive gradients through prediction of hidden sites; the new context loss directly matches their own outputs to clean teacher targets.

title: V-JEPA 2.1 · Targets
question: What is the target of V-JEPA 2.1 base self-supervision?
choices: A human noun label.
A robot action sequence.
A clean-input EMA teacher feature at the matching position and layer.
An RGB reconstruction produced by a fixed decoder.
explanation: Both masked and visible predictions match clean teacher features, with stop-gradient on targets.

title: V-JEPA 2.1 · Distance weights
question: With base coefficient 0.5, what is the context weight at distance 4?
explanation: The coefficient is 0.5 / sqrt(4) = 0.25. Distance weighting operates on context errors.

title: V-JEPA 2.1 · Separate counts
question: Context errors are 0.4 and 0.6 with weights 0.5 and 0.25. What is their context loss?
explanation: Divide the weighted error sum 0.20 + 0.15 by two context positions, not by the weight sum.

title: V-JEPA 2.1 · Deep supervision
question: How does deep self-supervision change training?
choices: It trains four unrelated encoders.
It removes clean teacher targets.
It matches both loss branches at four corresponding encoder levels.
It requires every downstream probe to concatenate four layers.
explanation: Intermediate and final feature levels receive predictive/context targets. Final-layer dense probes remain possible.

title: V-JEPA 2.1 · Native tokens
question: How many patch tokens come from a 16-frame 256×256 video with 16×16 patches and tubelet size 2?
explanation: Eight temporal positions times 16×16 spatial positions yields 2048 patch tokens, excluding any modality token convention.

title: V-JEPA 2.1 · Distillation EMA
question: Which network supplies the distillation loss targets?
choices: The student EMA.
The action-conditioned robot predictor.
An online EMA teacher updated from the small student.
A frozen ViT-G teacher.
explanation: Distillation uses a fixed ViT-G target; student EMA is maintained for the released encoder and never used in the loss.

title: V-JEPA 2.1 · Planning comparison
question: What qualifies the 60% to 80% grasp-success comparison?
choices: The 80% result also changes planning horizon and takes 14 seconds versus 3.
It proves a 20% relative gain for an identical planner.
It uses no action-data training.
All robot skills improve by 20 points.
explanation: At the same listed planner settings the gain is 60% to 70%; 80% uses a longer horizon and slower planning, over ten tasks per skill.

title: SAM 3 · Concept versus instance
question: What does a positive exemplar box mean in PCS?
choices: Find other instances matching the demonstrated concept.
Return only the pixels inside that box.
Delete all text tokens permanently.
Train a new model on this image.
explanation: A concept exemplar can affect the entire predicted set; PVS instead refines an indicated instance.

title: SAM 3 · Shared backbone
question: Which features feed the video memory-attention path?
choices: Only the semantic binary map.
Unconditioned PE frame features through a separate neck.
Only text tokens with no image features.
The final cgF1 evaluation score.
explanation: Detection conditions image features on prompts, while tracking separately conditions unconditioned PE features on per-object memory.

title: SAM 3 · Query slots
question: What are the 200 learned object queries?
choices: Exactly 200 user clicks.
A guaranteed set of 200 true objects.
Learned output slots that may be unmatched or duplicated.
The maximum text context length.
explanation: Queries propose objects; they are not input prompts or a guarantee of detection count.

title: SAM 3 · Presence gating
question: Presence is 0.8 and conditional query score is 0.7. What is the final score?
explanation: The same global presence factor multiplies every local conditional score: 0.8 × 0.7 = 0.56.

title: SAM 3 · Negative supervision
question: How is an absent concept supervised in the selected decoupled strategy?
choices: Train presence on absence; skip per-query classification for that pair.
Mark all queries positive.
Train only the tracker with no presence loss.
Always supervise the product and detach presence.
explanation: The presence branch learns absent concepts. Unmatched queries still receive negative labels on positive concept-image pairs.

title: SAM 3 · Training versus interaction
question: What changes during ordinary video inference?
choices: PE weights are optimized on every new frame.
Prompts, object IDs and memory state evolve with fixed learned weights.
An EMA teacher updates the presence token.
The cgF1 metric trains the mask decoder.
explanation: The tracker is learned in stage 4 with frozen PE; inference carries state without a user-label optimizer update.

title: SAM 3 · Track suppression
question: A confirmed track has negative lifetime MDS. What happens?
choices: Its state must be deleted permanently.
Every detector query is removed.
Its output is zeroed while its state remains available for recovery.
Its identity is merged with every new object.
explanation: Lifetime suppression retains state; removal of an unconfirmed candidate is a separate policy.

title: SAM 3 · Evidence
question: Why can presence improve cgF1 even when pmF1 falls?
choices: cgF1 is identical to mask AP.
cgF1 ignores absent concepts.
The human oracle becomes a training label.
Better image-level recognition can outweigh worse positive-mask localization.
explanation: cgF1 multiplies positive micro F1 by image-level MCC. Table 9a shows the two factors can move in different directions.
